content:
Just days before the much-anticipated release of Rockstar Games’ “Grand Theft Auto VI,” Fox News’ Rachel Campos-Duffy was roasted on social media for engaging in the conservative pastime of faux outrage over video games.

During Sunday’s edition of “Fox & Friends,” the hosts discussed the potential economic and cultural impacts of the game, slated for release on Nov. 19. A clip of Campos-Duffy, in which she maligns the game’s potential impact on society, then went viral on social media.

“I really am going to say I’m not thinking this is a good thing for our culture and society,” Campos-Duffy said. She also referred to the game’s female protagonist, Lucia, as a “hooker,” which her co-hosts quickly corrected.

Fans of the franchise jumped at the chance to scorn the hosts’ comments, calling out the apparent moral panic that often accompanies the release of high-profile video games featuring mature content.

Many critics pointed out that mainstream media outlets, including Fox News, had similar reactions when the franchise’s previous installment, “Grand Theft Auto V,” was released in 2013. Other users mocked the fact that Fox News has a parody version in the “GTA” universe known as “Weazel News.”

While Thursday’s release will likely spark more controversy as players enter the world of Vice City, the game is expected to shatter sales records. “Grand Theft Auto VI” will also be the first in the franchise’s history to feature a female protagonist.

According to Sensor Tower data, as of Tuesday, pre-order sales of the game had already surpassed 15 million and grossed over $1.5 billion.
